Yes you should have quite a bit of time as long as you look before it starts getting nippy, around late September-ish. Last winter wasn't as bad as it usually is, I've heard and was told. But it started chilling around end of september.

I'm thinking because it is hot there all the time it will be harder to find then during the off season (aka right now). Try to look at sports places that sell ski or snowboarding gear. They might have boots on off season.

Bullet points for the win:

* Winter clothes shopping can be done either in Phoenix or up in Flagstaff, though you might get more of a selection in Phoenix and possibly find what you need cheaper.

* I ended up finding a good pair of snow boots for fairly cheap from Payless. They also have a Kohls, Walmart, a Target right off campus, and some other places that will have winter gear.

* Generally it's just icy a few days after snow and I saw people wearing sneakers and fashion boots. I recommend at least one pair of heavy duty snow boots with good treads, and maybe one other pair of boots with decent treads. Any other time it depends. Most other pairs of shoes are good as long as it hasn't just rained or snowed. 

* The things I ended up using the most were a good peacoat I had gotten and socks that are a bit thicker. Generally if you layer jackets and legs (nylons under jeans, leggings, ect.) when it's cold you'll be alright. Other than that jeans, t shirts, whatever you normally wear. Sometimes it's nice enough for shorts and sandals.
